extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and writers interested in Audre Lorde, Black feminism, womanism, and creative/political practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles drawn from Audre Lorde's life and essays for writers and activists who want to apply her critiques of difference, identity, and power to creative or scholarly work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use human difference as creative springboard
rubrics_metrics.description: "We speak not of human difference, but of human deviance," she writes; differences should be used as a springboard for creative change rather than treated as deviance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lorde cautions against the "institutionalized rejection of difference" and urges that differences be developed as tools for creative change. Anti-pattern: pretending differences do not exist or dismissing them as 'deviance,' which robs creative work of energy and insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge the 'mythical norm'
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde argues that a mythical norm (in US culture: White, thin, male, young, heterosexual, Christian, financially secure) is what all bodies are expected to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative and critical work should be aware of and resist centring this mythical norm; representation and critique should expose and dismantle normative assumptions rather than replicate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address intersecting oppressions (multi-ism analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde defines racism, sexism, ageism, heterosexism, elitism and classism together and explains an 'ism' privileges one group over others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing identity or injustice to a single axis; attend to how multiple 'isms' interact in subjectivity and social structures. Anti-pattern: simplistic single-axis analysis that erases compound harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center womanist perspectives where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Womanism "allows Black women to affirm and celebrate their color and culture in a way that feminism does not."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with Black women's experience, center cultural specificity and celebration rather than folding those experiences into a generic (often white) feminism. Be attentive to the distinct aims and methods of womanist approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use personal experience as authorial authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde shows that one's authority to speak comes from one's experiences: "If I didn't define myself for myself, I would be crunched into other people's fantasies for me and eaten alive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage self-definition in writing; foreground lived experience as legitimate knowledge. Anti-pattern: allowing outside observers to define marginalized lives or silencing self-representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat difference as productive tension for creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Difference must be not merely tolerated, but seen as a fund of necessary polarities between which our creativity can spark like a dialectic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame difference as generative rather than threatening; use contrasts and plural perspectives to create dialectical creative energy instead of flattening or erasing differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage differences explicitly to avoid erasing bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignoring differences can lead to ignoring any bias and prejudice that might come with these differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly name and work through differences in text and practice; constructive engagement prevents blind spots. Anti-pattern: claiming neutrality by not acknowledging difference, which perpetuates bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new definitions of power and relations across difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde argued "we must... develop new definitions of power and new patterns of relating across difference. The old definitions have not served us."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid trying to dismantle oppression using the same exclusionary systems that produced it. Creative/political projects should imagine and model power relations that are non-hierarchical and cross-difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include marginalized literary forms and voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde found that "the literature of women of Color [was] seldom included..." and that poetry (often associated with lower class/working people) was rejected from women's magazine collectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial practice, curricula, and anthologies should actively include poetry and works by women of color; counteract gatekeeping that devalues genres or voices due to class, race, or form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit and accountable about sexuality in womanist/feminist work
rubrics_metrics.description: Womanism is criticized for its lack of discussion of sexuality; Lorde herself was open about her sexuality and embodied lesbian identity in her work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vagueness around sexuality when it is central to experience; be forthright in addressing sexual identity and politics rather than eliding them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confront internalized bias and transform it into political engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde urges individuals to "reach down into that deep place of knowledge inside herself and touch that terror and loathing of any difference that lives there... Then the personal as the political can begin to illuminate all our choices."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice introspection to recognize internalized prejudice; use that self-knowledge to inform overt political/creative action. Anti-pattern: avoidance of difficult self-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize anti-racist coalition-building over intra-group conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde insists that the fight between Black women and men must end to end racist politics and that Black women's ties are not inherently antagonistic to Black men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In writing and activism, avoid framing intra-marginalized-group tensions as the central problem; instead, situate such tensions within broader racist/patriarchal systems and work toward coalition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use lived identities to educate and produce transformative work
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde used her interlocking identities (womanhood, gayness, blackness) within her work to create pieces that educated people about the issues Black lesbian women face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on intersectional lived experience to make work that both represents and teaches; do not suppress salient identities for palatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach difference with curiosity and aim for equality, not hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: People have reacted to difference by ignoring, conforming, or destroying; Lorde suggests approaching differences with curiosity or understanding and a 'third option of equality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame engagements across difference around mutual respect and equality rather than assimilation or dominance. Anti-pattern: forcing conformity or erasing distinctiveness in the name of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice 'politics of location'—specify context and particularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde and contemporaries called for a 'feminist politics of location' theorizing that women are subject to particular assemblies of oppression and thus emerge with particular, not generic, identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In scholarship and creative work, specify geographic, cultural, and historical context rather than relying on universalizing claims. Anti-pattern: abstracting 'women' or 'oppressed people' into a single undifferentiated category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cultural homogenization and othering of Global South women
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde warned that cultural homogenization of third-world women could lead to a disguised form of oppression and 'othering' women in developing nations into figures of deviance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize unique histories and power structures of women in developing countries; do not flatten diverse experiences into a single narrative or speak for them without context and specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build solidarity across difference without forcing sameness
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde affirmed that 'we do not have to become copies of each other to be able to work together' and that diversity gives power when joined across differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster coalition work that preserves difference while mobilizing shared goals; resist models of unity that require erasure of distinct identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rhetorical anger productively to expose systemic hatred
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorde identified 'anger, marginalized communities, and US culture' as themes and used communication techniques to shift subjectivities of White feminist audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat anger as a generative rhetorical and political resource to reveal oppression and motivate change rather than dismissing it as merely emotional. Anti-pattern: silencing anger as illegitimate and thereby maintaining the status quo.
